title: Evaluating a RAG system
description: Separate evidence-retrieval failures from unsupported answer generation.
objectives: Score citations and abstentions separately from retrieval
explanation: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately before scoring the full application. For each test question, identify the relevant source passages and whether the corpus can answer it. Retrieval recall at k measures how many known relevant passages occur in the first k results; ranking also matters when context is limited.

For generated answers, check whether claims are supported, whether cited sources actually support them, and whether the response addresses the question. A citation that points to a real document can still support the wrong claim. Include contradictory, outdated, and deliberately unanswerable cases.

Keep a fixed corpus snapshot and query set when comparing chunking or retrieval changes. Inspect per-case disagreements rather than just averaging a score. Combine clear automated checks with human review; a model judge can be inconsistent and should be calibrated against examples with known judgments.

terms.definition: Fraction of known relevant items retrieved among the first k results.
Whether answer claims are supported by supplied evidence.
Explicitly declining to answer when the available evidence is insufficient.

example: Three known passages answer a policy question. The top five results contain two, so recall at five is 2/3. If the answer invents a deadline absent from those passages, that is an answer-support failure even though retrieval partly succeeded.
mistakes: Measuring only whether an answer sounds helpful.
Counting any citation as proof of support.
Testing only questions known to have answers.
exercise: Create five answerable and three unanswerable questions over invented documents. Record supporting passage IDs, retrieved IDs, answer claims, and citation judgments. Run retrieval_metrics.py to check a toy recall calculation.

code.title: Recall over known relevant passage IDs

questions.question: What does retrieval recall at k measure?
questions.answer: The fraction of known relevant passages found within the first k results.
questions.distractor: The fraction of generated sentences containing punctuation.

questions.question: What belongs in an evidence-labeled RAG test case?
questions.answer: The query, corpus snapshot, relevant passage IDs, and whether an answer is supported.

questions.question: A correct document is retrieved but the answer adds an invented date. Which stage failed?
questions.answer: Generation or grounding failed even if retrieval found useful evidence.
questions.distractor: Retrieval must be perfect whenever an answer is fluent.

questions.question: Why include questions with no supporting passage in a RAG evaluation?
questions.answer: To measure whether the system abstains instead of manufacturing unsupported answers.
questions.distractor: To ensure every question receives a confident answer.

questions.question: Is a real citation URL sufficient evidence of faithfulness?
questions.answer: No. The cited passage must support the associated claim.
questions.distractor: Yes, any working URL proves the sentence.
